tweets.text:
Everyone is obsessed with making AI smarter. Almost nobody is talking about the fact that their AI keeps forgetting everything they teach it.

Claude Code can become something much more interesting than a coding assistant.

A second brain that remembers your projects, decisions, people and notes across sessions.

Here's how to build it:

1. Create a folder called SECOND BRAIN
2. Open Claude Code inside it
3. Add four folders: MEMORY/, notes/, people/, projects/
4. Create a CLAUDE.md that tells Claude how to organize and retrieve important information
5. Use @-imports to load your most important memory files at startup
6. Tell Claude to save key decisions as Markdown files, one topic per file
7. Create a custom /brain skill to search your notes and bring relevant context back

Now watch the video.

Every branch represents stored knowledge. The glowing line visualizes a memory being retrieved.

Something you decided weeks ago can become useful context in a completely new session.

No vector database. No expensive memory app. Just Markdown files and Claude Code.

The crazy part? Your knowledge doesn't have to disappear when the conversation ends.

Full SECOND BRAIN setup in the article below.

tweets.text:
I went through AI Engineer job posts on LinkedIn.

Almost every one asks for the same thing: proof you can make AI work in production not just in a notebook.

Here are 15 AI engineering projects that will make your resume stand out:

• RAG chatbot over 1,000+ real documents with source citations
• Agent that books, cancels and reschedules using real APIs
• AI coding assistant that writes tests for an existing repo
• Voice agent that answers calls and logs every conversation
• Model router that sends easy questions to a cheap model and hard ones to a smart one
• Semantic search engine for a real product catalog
• Document extractor that turns messy PDFs into clean JSON
• Fine-tuned small model that beats a big model on one narrow task
• LLM cost tracker showing spend per user and per feature
• Caching layer that cuts repeat API calls and latency
• Agent memory system that remembers users across sessions
• Evals suite that catches regressions before every deploy
• Tracing dashboard that shows every step an agent took
• Fallback system that retries, switches models and never shows users an error
• Red-team script that tries to jailbreak your own app

Pick 2–3.
Ship them to real users.
Post the numbers: cost, speed, accuracy.

That's your resume.

Bookmark this and send it to someone trying to break into AI engineering.

tweets.text:
Built Claude Code Clone – A Terminal-Based AI Coding Assistant

Built Claude Code Clone, a fully functional terminal based AI coding assistant inspired by Claude Code, It has 60+ tools in total and recreated from scratch using Gemini 2.5 Flash, LangGraph, and Model Context Protocol (MCP).
It uses LangGraph to manage multistep reasoning and PostgreSQL to preserve chat and tool history just like a persistent IDE assistant.

Integrated MCP Tools:
- Filesystem: Read, write, and search project files
- GitHub: Repo access, issues, and PR management (token supported)
- Web Search: Integrated via Tavily MCP server

Key Features:
- LangGraph-based state machine for structured multi-step workflows
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) for universal tool integration
- Persistent memory with PostgreSQL + Prisma

GitHub: https://t.co/EM3BOo6yUd (Give it a ⭐if you like the project!)

Tech Stack:
TypeScript, Node.js, Gemini API, LangGraph.js, MCP (Filesystem, GitHub, Tavily Search), PostgreSQL, Prisma ORM)
